title: 17.1: Sensor-Less Laser Voltage-Probing Attack Detection via Run-Time-Leakage-Shift Monitoring with 4.35% Area Overhead
problem: Laser voltage probing (LVP) attacks on integrated circuits achieve near-100% success rate by probing on-chip voltages through backside laser illumination with high spatial resolution and low cost. Current detection approaches lack effective sensor-less mechanisms to counter these physical attacks in cost-constrained systems.
motivation: Rising physical attack threats demand efficient detection/counteraction mechanisms, especially in low-cost and power-constrained silicon systems where area overhead must be minimized.
method: The design uses run-time leakage-shift monitoring to detect laser-induced anomalies without dedicated attack sensors. By observing shifts in device leakage currents caused by photocurrent injection during LVP attacks, the circuit can trigger countermeasures with minimal area overhead (4.35%).
key_novelty: Sensor-less detection of LVP attacks exploiting run-time leakage-shift signatures without requiring photodiodes or dedicated sensing infrastructure.
contributions: Achieves near-complete LVP attack detection without dedicated attack sensors
Minimal 4.35% area overhead compared to unprotected baseline
Run-time monitoring enables detection of attacks with spatial resolution below ~10μm
Practical for low-cost and power-constrained security applications
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; lock-in dynamics and false-positive rates from thermal/mechanical drifts not characterized.
primary_theme: Sensor-less hardware security via leakage monitoring
